About the studio

I’m learning by making applications.

SeedCore began with deep questions about how software acts in the real world. Today I’m bringing those ideas closer to people: a city guide, a family journey, a souvenir studio, a collector experience and a friendly robot moment.

The short version

I’m not presenting myself as a giant platform company or an abstract engineering expert. I’m an independent builder working through concrete application ideas, one useful experience at a time.

What connects the work

A place to understand. Something to create. A next step to trust.

Places

Make a city feel discoverable.

I’m interested in local makers, workshops, attractions and public stories that are difficult to find through a generic search box.

People

Give families a real role.

Children can make choices and create. Parents keep approval, privacy and payment. The product should feel joyful to both.

Real things

Help the physical story stay clear.

Whether it is a rare shoe, a souvenir or a robot action, the application should help a person understand what they are seeing and what happens next.

My working style

Begin with a small moment that can be tested.

I prefer a working city slice over a giant city promise, one five-minute souvenir flow over a generic creator platform, and one understandable handover over a broad story about autonomous commerce.

01

Prototype the experience.

Make the journey visible enough for a real person to react to it.

02

Label the truth.

Say clearly what is a prototype, what is a pilot design and what is still only an idea.

03

Earn the next layer.

Add complexity only when it makes the application safer, clearer or more useful.

Let’s talk

If one of these application worlds overlaps with yours, I’d like to hear the story.
